meta.description: A short guide for business owners: 3 rules for the first second of an AI video, and which video fits restaurants, real estate, music and events, and brands and sport. With real examples and numbers.

guide.home_entry: New · Free guide: which AI video will bring customers to your business

hero.lead: Most business AI videos open on a logo, and viewers scroll past before they know what they're watching. On my page, a video that opens on an ice cream tub from the freezer reached {icecream} views, {ratio} times the median Reel on this site. Films that open on a logo get, on average, a small fraction of that.
hero.stat_icecream: A video that opens on an ice cream tub from the freezer
hero.stat_ratio: the median Reel on this site
hero.after: The difference isn't budget or tools. It's what the viewer sees in the first second.

items.title: Open on something your customer knows, not your logo
items.body: Viewers decide within a second whether to stay. A logo tells them nothing. Something they know from home, the supermarket line or their phone tells them: this is about me.
items.example: An ice cream tub that's in almost every Israeli freezer, right in the first frame.

items.title: The twist lands in the first second
items.body: Once they recognize it, surprise them, and fast. A surprise at second five arrives when they're already on the next video.
items.example: It opens on the ending: a guy walks out of a 7-Eleven with half a shelf. Only then do you learn he went in for a bottle of water.

items.title: Your brand comes in after you've hooked them
items.body: Your product isn't the hook. It's the answer. Once the viewer is curious, the brand closes the story instead of opening it.
items.example: First the face of someone hearing "139 shekels?!". Only then does the cake box open.

items.name: Restaurants and food
items.what: A moment every customer has had with the dish or the price: the argument over the price, the first bite, what's left in the box.
items.gets: Shares and tags: people sending it to the friend who argues over every price, so your dish joins the conversation.

items.name: Real estate
items.what: The moment everyone who has hunted for an apartment knows: apartment number 15, and the argument over what you'll give up this time.
items.gets: People hunting for an apartment right now see themselves in it, and the project stays with them when they reach the next step.

items.name: Music and events
items.what: A look at what happens before the audience arrives: rehearsals, backstage, the moment something went wrong.
items.gets: Buzz before the event: the audience feeling they're seeing something that isn't out yet.

items.name: Brands and sport
items.what: The team's or the brand's news moment, on the day it happens: a signing, a launch, a win.
